rounds.text: The valuation is stretched far beyond what fundamentals support, highlighted by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 2 per share against a market price of Rs 12.2, which leaves a margin of safety at a staggering -577.5% [E44, E45]. The reverse DCF reveals that today’s price already bakes in an unrealistic 32.6% earnings growth expectation compared to the modest 6.0% assumed in the base case [E46]. Long-term top-line erosion is evident with a 10-year compounded sales growth of -1% and a -5% contraction over the trailing twelve months, proving that recent profit spikes are decoupled from structural revenue expansion [E14, E17]. Furthermore, institutional investors are fleeing, registering negative money flow with foreign holdings dropping to 0.60% and domestic institutional holdings completely wiped out to 0.00% [E41, E42, E43]. Historical wealth destruction is extreme, underscored by a catastrophic worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -99.6% and negative median ROE figures stretching across 10, 5, and 3-year horizons [E26, E27, E28, E52]. Conceded: the quarterly operating margin reached 43% in March 2026 alongside a significant improvement in debtor days from 79.1 to 60.3 [E31, E58].
